context.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening Platform screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud at 3,000 TPS while enabling analysts to review suspicious transactions. It ensures sub-50ms latency, PCI-DSS compliance, and a 7-year tamper-evident audit trail within a €25k monthly AWS budget.

## Key Elements
*   **Payment Gateway / Acquirer**: Upstream actor submitting authorization requests.
*   **Fraud Analyst & Risk Manager**: Internal users reviewing cases and monitoring fraud metrics.
*   **Corporate Identity Provider (IdP)**: Authenticates analysts via OIDC/SAML.
*   **Card Tokenization Provider**: External vault for PCI-DSS scope reduction.
*   **Notification Gateway**: External SMS/Email service (Amazon SES/Twilio) for alerts.
*   **Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening Platform**: Core AWS-hosted system containerized on ECS Fargate.

## Relationships
*   **Payment Gateway** -> *Sends Authorization Requests (gRPC/HTTPS via AWS PrivateLink and NLB)* -> **Fraud Screening Platform**
*   **Fraud Analyst** -> *Reviews cases and tunes rules (HTTPS via ALB)* -> **Fraud Screening Platform**
*   **Fraud Screening Platform** -> *Authenticates users (OIDC/SAML)* -> **Corporate IdP**
*   **Fraud Screening Platform** -> *Sends operational alerts (HTTPS)* -> **Notification Gateway**

## Technology Stack
*   **Compute**: Amazon ECS with AWS Fargate to eliminate node management toil for a 3-person team.
*   **Networking**: AWS Network Load Balancer (NLB) with AWS PrivateLink for sub-50ms P99 latency.
*   **Audit & Storage**: AWS QLDB or S3 Object Lock for tamper-evident 7-year audit logs.
*   **Deployment**: GitOps (ArgoCD) for zero-downtime model and rule updates.

## Rationale
This architecture uses serverless containers and private networking to meet strict performance and PCI-DSS requirements without excessive operational overhead. The lean AWS stack stays comfortably within the €25k monthly budget while supporting a 3-person engineering team.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
The system is a Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening Platform that screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud and manages analyst case reviews. It ensures high throughput, strict security, and regulatory compliance for mid-size payment processors.

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analyst & Risk Manager (Users)
- Payment Gateway / Acquirer, Corporate Identity Provider (IdP), Card Tokenization Provider, Notification Gateway (External Systems)
- API Gateway (AWS API Gateway - HTTP APIs)
- Scoring Engine Container (Go, ONNX runtime, Amazon ECS on AWS Fargate)
- Case Management Container (Next.js / Node.js, Amazon ECS on AWS Fargate)
- Data Stores & Messaging: Amazon RDS PostgreSQL, Amazon S3 (WORM Object Lock & Model Bucket), Amazon SQS / EventBridge, Amazon Kinesis / S3 Data Lake
- Analytics & Discovery: Amazon Athena, AWS Cloud Map

## Relationships
- Payment Gateway to API Gateway via mTLS
- API Gateway to Scoring Engine Container via gRPC over HTTP/2
- Scoring Engine Container to Amazon S3 (Model Bucket) via HTTPS with digital signature verification
- Case Management Container to Amazon RDS PostgreSQL via TLS
- Case Management Container to Amazon SQS / EventBridge via AWS SDK
- Athena to Amazon S3 WORM Bucket via SQL queries for audit reports

## Technology Stack
- AWS ECS on AWS Fargate: Chosen for zero-overhead container orchestration fitting a 3-engineer team and €25k budget.
- Go & ONNX Runtime: Selected for the Scoring Engine to achieve sub-10ms P99 latency at 3,000 TPS.
- Next.js (Node.js) & Amazon RDS PostgreSQL: Chosen for rapid Case Management UI development and relational case tracking.
- Amazon S3 with Object Lock & Athena: Implemented for tamper-evident, 7-year audit retention and cost-effective compliance reporting.

## Rationale
This architecture meets sub-50ms latency and high-throughput requirements using lightweight Go containers and Fargate while maintaining PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance. It operates securely within a €25,000 monthly budget managed by three engineers.

API Gateway.analysis:
## Overview
- Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system evaluating card-not-present payment authorizations for a mid-size payment processor.
- Screens transactions for fraud, manages analyst review cases, and ensures PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance with sub-50ms P99 latency.

## Key Elements
- Payment Gateway / Acquirer (External System)
- Fraud Analyst & Risk Manager (Users)
- Corporate IdP (External System)
- AWS API Gateway (Container - HTTP APIs)
- Scoring Engine Container (Container - Amazon ECS on AWS Fargate)
- Case Management Container (Container - Amazon ECS on AWS Fargate)
- Amazon S3 WORM Bucket (Container - Amazon S3 with Object Lock)
- Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose (Container)

## Relationships
- Payment Gateway / Acquirer -> AWS API Gateway: Sends payment authorization requests [mTLS]
- Fraud Analyst & Risk Manager -> AWS API Gateway: Accesses Case Management UI [HTTPS via ALB]
- AWS API Gateway -> Scoring Engine Container: Routes authorization scoring requests [/v1/authorize via gRPC over HTTP/2]
- AWS API Gateway -> Case Management Container: Routes analyst management requests [/v1/cases via HTTPS]
- AWS API Gateway -> Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose: Streams compressed access logs for auditability [AWS Native Integration]
- Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose -> Amazon S3 WORM Bucket: Persists tamper-evident transaction logs for 7 years [AWS Native Integration]

## Technology Stack
- AWS API Gateway (HTTP APIs): Manages ingress, TLS termination, and path segregation with minimal operational overhead.
- Amazon ECS on AWS Fargate: Runs stateless scoring and case management containers, matching the 3-engineer team capacity.
- Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose: Provides batching and compression for zero-code telemetry without Lambda latency on the critical path.
- Amazon S3 WORM Bucket (Object Lock): Implements tamper-evident storage to meet the 7-year audit retention constraint.

## Rationale
- Managed AWS services minimize operational complexity, allowing a 3-engineer team to maintain the platform within the 25,000 EUR monthly budget.
- Path segregation and native API Gateway integrations protect the sub-50ms P99 latency threshold for 3,000 req/s while satisfying PCI-DSS and audit mandates.

Scoring Engine Container.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system evaluates card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud to protect merchant revenue while complying with PCI-DSS Level 1. It screens transactions in real time, routes suspicious payments for analyst review, and securely audits all decisions.

## Key Elements
- **API Gateway**: AWS API Gateway (HTTP APIs) routing requests.
- **Scoring Engine Container**: Go and ONNX runtime running on Amazon ECS on AWS Fargate.
  - **API Router Component**: Handles gRPC-over-HTTP/2 requests and timeouts.
  - **Feature Enrichment Component**: Fetches velocity features via AWS ElastiCache (Redis `cache.t4g.micro`).
  - **Model Execution Engine**: Evaluates transactions using concurrent double-buffered models.
  - **Fallback & Circuit Breaker Component**: Enforces R-07 availability constraints.
  - **Audit & Telemetry Dispatcher**: Asynchronously flushes tamper-evident audit logs.
- **Storage & Auditing**: Amazon RDS PostgreSQL, Amazon S3 WORM Bucket & Model Bucket, Amazon SQS / EventBridge with DLQ, and Amazon Athena & S3 Data Lake.

## Relationships
- **API Gateway -> Scoring Engine Container**: Routes authorization scoring requests via gRPC over HTTP/2.
- **API Router Component -> Feature Enrichment Component**: Invokes feature lookup via Go interface.
- **Feature Enrichment Component -> Model Execution Engine**: Passes enriched feature vector via Go struct.
- **Model Execution Engine -> Fallback Component**: Intercepts timeouts and errors via Go context.
- **Scoring Engine Container -> Amazon S3 WORM Bucket & Model Bucket**: Loads models and uploads tamper-signed audit payloads via HTTPS with digital signatures.
- **Scoring Engine Container -> Amazon SQS / EventBridge**: Dispatches telemetry and audit records asynchronously.

## Technology Stack
- **Go (`net/http`)**: High-performance backend language chosen to meet the <50ms P99 latency requirement.
- **ONNX Runtime (C-Bindings)**: Executes compiled machine learning models in memory with zero-downtime hot-swapping.
- **Amazon ECS on AWS Fargate**: Container orchestration providing scalable compute within a fixed budget.
- **AWS ElastiCache (Redis `cache.t4g.micro`)**: Low-latency sliding-window feature store fitting the 25,000 EUR monthly budget.
- **Amazon S3 Object Lock**: Ensures 7-year tamper-evident auditability for compliance.

## Rationale
This architecture uses Go and ONNX on AWS Fargate to consistently deliver sub-50ms decision latencies at high throughput. It satisfies strict PCI-DSS Level 1 security, tamper-evident 7-year auditability, and zero-downtime model updates within a 25,000 EUR monthly budget operated by a 3-engineer team.

Case Management Container.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system screens card-not-present payment authorizations in the cloud before approval and provides case management tools for fraud analysts. It operates on AWS within a strict compliance, budget, and team size framework.

## Key Elements
* Fraud Analysts & Risk Managers
* AWS API Gateway (HTTP APIs)
* Scoring Engine Container (Go, ONNX runtime, Amazon ECS on Amazon Fargate)
* Case Management Frontend (Static SPA on Amazon S3 and Amazon CloudFront)
* Case Management Backend (Node.js API on Amazon ECS on Amazon Fargate)
* Amazon RDS PostgreSQL
* Amazon S3 WORM Bucket & Model Bucket
* Amazon SQS / Amazon EventBridge
* External Systems: Payment Gateway / Acquirer, Corporate Identity Provider (IdP), Card Tokenization Provider, Notification Gateway

## Relationships
* Payment Gateway / Acquirer -> AWS API Gateway: Submits authorization requests [HTTPS]
* AWS API Gateway -> Scoring Engine Container: Routes scoring requests [HTTP/JSON]
* AWS API Gateway -> Case Management Backend: Routes analyst requests [HTTPS]
* Case Management Frontend (S3/CloudFront) -> Case Management Backend: Invokes REST API [HTTPS]
* Case Management Backend -> Amazon RDS PostgreSQL: Reads and writes case data, prioritizations, and audits [TLS]
* Case Management Backend -> Amazon S3 WORM Bucket: Streams tamper-evident audit logs [AWS SDK / HTTPS]
* Case Management Backend -> Amazon SQS / Amazon EventBridge: Publishes asynchronous events [AWS SDK]
* Case Management Backend -> Notification Gateway: Dispatches operational alerts [HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
* AWS Cloud (eu-west-1 region): Selected to meet regional compliance and infrastructure requirements.
* Amazon ECS on AWS Fargate: Runs containerized services without managing underlying servers, fitting the 3-engineer constraint.
* Node.js & Next.js (Static SPA): Powers the analyst UI decoupled from the backend for optimized cost and performance.
* Go & ONNX Runtime: Powers the high-performance scoring engine to achieve sub-50ms P99 latency.
* Amazon RDS PostgreSQL: Stores relational case data and transactional records securely.
* Amazon S3 WORM Bucket (Object Lock): Ensures tamper-evident, 7-year auditability for regulatory compliance.

## Rationale
This architecture balances stringent PCI-DSS Level 1 security and 7-year auditability with high-performance real-time scoring. Decoupling the static SPA frontend from the lean Fargate backend optimizes operational efficiency for a three-engineer team within the 25,000 EUR monthly budget.

Amazon RDS PostgreSQL.analysis:
## Overview
Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening screens card-not-present payment authorizations for a mid-size payment processor using AWS. It processes transactions to approve, decline, or flag them while supporting analyst case management.

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analysts & Risk Managers
- API Gateway (AWS API Gateway - HTTP APIs)
- Scoring Engine Container (Go, ONNX runtime, Amazon ECS on AWS Fargate)
- Case Management Container (Next.js / Node.js, Amazon ECS on AWS Fargate)
- Amazon RDS PostgreSQL (Database with schemas: `cases_db`, `audit_log`, PgBouncer/RDS Proxy)
- Amazon S3 WORM Bucket & Model Bucket (Amazon S3 with WORM Object Lock)
- AWS Lambda & Amazon EventBridge (Audit log archival pipeline)
- Supporting Services: Amazon SQS, Amazon Athena, AWS Secrets Manager, AWS KMS

## Relationships
- Case Management Container -> Amazon RDS PostgreSQL: Reads and writes case and audit data via SQL over [TLS 1.3] with IAM Database Authentication
- AWS Lambda -> Amazon RDS PostgreSQL & Amazon S3 WORM Bucket: Exports and purges audit partitions older than 90 days via scheduled [HTTPS]
- Amazon RDS PostgreSQL -> Amazon CloudWatch: Streams `pgaudit` logs and performance metrics over [HTTPS]
- Fraud Analysts -> API Gateway / Case Management Container: Reviews flagged payments via secure web interface over [HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
- Amazon RDS PostgreSQL: Relational database chosen for low operational overhead and ACID compliance, fitting the 3-engineer team constraint
- AWS RDS Proxy / PgBouncer: Connection pooling to handle high-concurrency connection spikes and prevent backend exhaustion
- PostgreSQL `pgaudit` & Trigger-Based RLS: Enforces least privilege, row-level security, and immutable audit logs for PCI-DSS compliance
- Amazon S3 with WORM Object Lock: Cost-effective long-term storage for 7-year tamper-evident audit logs within the 25,000 EUR/month budget

## Rationale
This architecture meets PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year audit requirements securely through immutable S3 offloading and RDS security controls. It stays within budget and team limits by utilizing managed AWS services and automated data lifecycles.

Amazon S3 WORM Bucket & Model Bucket.analysis:
## Overview
[Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening Platform] provides card-not-present fraud scoring and analyst case management for a mid-size payment processor. It screens payment authorizations in real-time while maintaining strict compliance, auditability, and cost constraints.

## Key Elements
* Fraud Analyst & Risk Manager (Users)
* Payment Gateway / Acquirer, Corporate Identity Provider (IdP), Card Tokenization Provider, Notification Gateway (External Systems)
* API Gateway (AWS API Gateway - HTTP APIs)
* Scoring Engine Container (Go, ONNX runtime, Amazon ECS on AWS Fargate)
* Case Management Container (Next.js / Node.js, Amazon ECS on AWS Fargate)
* Amazon RDS PostgreSQL (Database)
* Amazon S3 WORM Bucket & Model Bucket (Amazon S3 with WORM Object Lock & Versioning)
* Amazon SQS / EventBridge (Messaging/Events)
* Amazon Athena & S3 Data Lake (Analytics)

## Relationships
* API Gateway -> Scoring Engine Container [HTTPS/REST]
* API Gateway -> Case Management Container [HTTPS/REST]
* Scoring Engine Container -> Amazon RDS PostgreSQL [TCP/PostgreSQL protocol]
* Scoring Engine Container -> Amazon S3 WORM Bucket & Model Bucket [HTTPS (TLS 1.3), AWS IAM SigV4, VPC Gateway Endpoints]
* Case Management Container -> Amazon RDS PostgreSQL [TCP/PostgreSQL protocol]
* Amazon Athena & S3 Data Lake -> Amazon S3 WORM Bucket & Model Bucket [SQL queries, HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
* AWS (eu-west-1): Target cloud provider ensuring managed scalability and low latency.
* Go & ONNX Runtime: Powers the Scoring Engine for high performance and sub-50ms P99 latency.
* Next.js / Node.js: Powers the Case Management interface for analysts.
* Amazon RDS PostgreSQL: Relational storage for application data and case workflows.
* Amazon S3 (WORM Object Lock & Versioning): Secure, immutable storage meeting the 7-year audit requirement.
* Terraform: Infrastructure-as-Code for automated, drift-free deployments managed by a 3-person team.

## Rationale
[The microservices and serverless-leaning AWS architecture delivers sub-50ms P99 latency at 3,000 requests per second while strictly adhering to the €25,000 monthly budget. Immutable S3 storage and strict IAM boundaries ensure PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year tamper-evident auditability.]

Amazon SQS / EventBridge.analysis:
## Overview
[The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening Platform screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud and manages suspicious cases. It ensures secure, low-latency decision-making while meeting strict compliance and audit requirements.]

## Key Elements
* [Scoring Engine Container (Go, ONNX runtime, Amazon ECS on AWS Fargate)]
* [Case Management Container (Next.js / Node.js, Amazon ECS on AWS Fargate)]
* [Amazon SQS Case Queue (Standard/FIFO)]
* [EventBridge Audit Bus (Custom Event Bus with Archive and Replay)]
* [Amazon S3 WORM Bucket & Data Lake]
* [AWS KMS Customer Managed Keys (CMK)]

## Relationships
* [Scoring Engine Container -> SQS Case Queue: SendMessage [AWS SDK / HTTPS]]
* [SQS Case Queue -> Case Management Container: ReceiveMessage [AWS SDK / HTTPS]]
* [Scoring Engine Container -> EventBridge Audit Bus: PutEvents [AWS SDK / HTTPS]]
* [EventBridge Audit Bus -> Amazon Athena & S3 Data Lake: Firehose / S3 Target [AWS Native / HTTPS]]

## Technology Stack
* [Amazon ECS on AWS Fargate: Provides serverless container orchestration to minimize infrastructure management for a 3-engineer team.]
* [Amazon SQS: Handles asynchronous, point-to-point case queuing with Dead Letter Queues to guarantee at-least-once delivery.]
* [Amazon EventBridge: Manages fan-out event distribution and immutable 7-year audit logging via Archive and Replay.]
* [AWS KMS CMK: Enforces strong at-rest encryption to satisfy PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance requirements.]

## Rationale
[This architecture decouples synchronous, low-latency scoring from heavy asynchronous auditing to meet the P99 <50ms performance requirement. Furthermore, leveraging fully managed AWS services keeps operational overhead minimal for a three-engineer team within the 25,000 EUR monthly budget.]

Amazon Athena & S3 Data Lake.analysis:
## Overview
[The Amazon Athena & S3 Data Lake container provides serverless analytics and immutable storage for compliance auditing, risk reporting, and fraud trend analysis. It securely ingests transaction logs to satisfy 7-year audit mandates while keeping operational costs within the fixed infrastructure budget.]

## Key Elements
* Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose
* Amazon S3 Data Lake Storage (Raw and Curated Zones with S3 Object Lock)
* AWS Glue Data Catalog
* Amazon Athena Query Engine
* AWS Lake Formation

## Relationships
* Scoring Engine & Case Management Containers -> Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose: Ingests transaction logs [HTTPS / AWS SDK]
* Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose -> Amazon S3 Data Lake Storage: Batch-writes logs in Apache Parquet format [S3 API]
* AWS Glue Data Catalog -> Amazon S3 Data Lake Storage: Maintains schema definitions [Internal AWS API]
* Amazon Athena Query Engine -> AWS Glue Data Catalog: Reads metadata for query execution [Internal AWS API]
* Risk Managers & BI Tools -> Amazon Athena Query Engine: Executes compliance audits and trend queries [JDBC/ODBC / HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
* Amazon S3: Chosen for cost-effective, durable storage with Object Lock compliance mode for immutable 7-year audit retention.
* Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose: Selected for near-real-time streaming ingestion and automated conversion to Apache Parquet format.
* AWS Glue Data Catalog: Utilized for automated schema discovery and cataloging of analytical datasets.
* Amazon Athena: Chosen for serverless, pay-per-query SQL execution minimizing idle infrastructure costs.
* AWS Lake Formation: Deployed to enforce column-level data masking and fine-grained access control for PCI-DSS compliance.

## Rationale
[This architecture satisfies PCI-DSS Level 1 and 7-year audit requirements through immutable S3 Object Lock and strict Lake Formation access controls. It respects the €25,000 monthly budget by leveraging serverless Athena queries and Parquet storage optimization.]
